title: doctor advises molt resleeve where only a login clears the env check's finding, and the env liberator's PATH refusal names zshrc where .zprofile builds PATH
body:
Found at Molt 1.2.0's rollout, 30 Oct 2026, on kovacs (kovacs-sysadm) and on rhadamanth.

When the env check fails only because the GUI session does not hold a published pair, its own remedy says that only a login clears it. That session is launchd's GUI domain on macOS (issue 0072) and the systemd user manager on Linux (issue 0076). On macOS the remedy is the next login or a bootstrap of com.molt.env, and on Linux it is to log out and back in. Doctor's enabled-liberator check then reports env as "not installed", and closes with its fixed hint (lib/molt.sh, cmd_doctor): "Run `molt resleeve` to install, or `molt list` for status." A resleeve renders the same files again and changes nothing the session holds, so the hint sends the reader to a step that cannot clear the finding. kovacs-sysadm read it that way on kovacs, where the manager held a PATH without ~/.local/bin and with /snap/bin twice until hv's GNOME re-login. rhadamanth showed the same, with launchd lacking INTENT_INSTALL_PREFIX because the plist is newer than the last login.

Ask: doctor names `molt resleeve` only where a resleeve would clear what failed. When the only finding is one the env check says a login clears, it names env as published but not yet in the session, and leaves the remedy to the env check's own line. Doctor still fails on it, since GUI apps really do not get the value (issue 0059).

A second remedy names the wrong place, found at issue 0079's review on 1 Nov 2026 (molt-vc). When a login shell's PATH does not start with ~/.local/bin, the env liberator's refusal (molt_env_path_pair in lib/env.sh, line 204 today) says to put ~/.local/bin first on PATH in zshrc. Molt-matts has built PATH in .zprofile since issue 0076, and Molt-flynn since issue 0079, so the remedy names the wrong file. The liberator reads PATH from `zsh -lic` (lib/env.sh:175-176), which reads .zshrc after .zprofile, so .zshrc can still put a directory ahead of ~/.local/bin: Flynn's zshrc runs mise activate, which puts mise's shims first (issue 0079's as-built note). Ask: the refusal names .zprofile as the file that puts ~/.local/bin first, and says nothing in .zshrc may prepend ahead of it.

Not in 1.2.0: hv ruled one release today, with no new work for its own sake (vc decisions 36 and 38).


## As built (dc, 3 Nov 2026; reviewed and accepted by vc at c8b46f3 and ce168ef)

- `lib/liberator.sh`: `MOLT_CHECK_SESSION_PENDING` is the status a check returns when what it installs is in place, as molt would write it, and only the session a login sets up does not hold it yet.
- `env_check` returns it only when its refusals and file faults are clean and the session report found a pair the session lacks. `molt_env_report_session` returns 2 for a session it cannot read, which stays a plain failure.
- `cmd_doctor` keeps each check's status. Its verdict names "published, not yet in the session" apart from "not installed", it prints the resleeve hint only when something is not installed, and it still fails.
- Every other caller treats the new status as any failure, unchanged: `liberator_status_all`, `cmd_list` and `molt_resleeve`.
- Doctor shows a failing check's first `MOLT_DOCTOR_CHECK_LINES` lines and, when it printed more, how many it left out and its last line (ce168ef). Since 0078, a pending env with three findings had shown no remedy at all; that regression was caught at vc's review.
- The env liberator's PATH refusal names `.zprofile`, and says nothing in `.zshrc` may prepend ahead of `~/.local/bin`.
- Tests: `env.bats` and `molt.bats` name the status by its constant, and the doctor tests derive every count from the fixture or the constant. vc's runs: env.bats and molt.bats pass under Homebrew bash 5.3.20 and /bin/bash 3.2.57. shellcheck -x and intent critic shell are clean.
- Docs: `docs/guides/sleeve-agents.md`, and CHANGELOG Unreleased (Fixed). Ships in Molt 1.4.0 (vc decision 44).
